source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Houston campus is the largest data center in Texas that publishes a power figure, at 84 MW, yet 114 of the state's 133 mapped facilities disclose nothing.

The 84 MW across HOU3 and HOU4 is 18 percent of the 475 MW that 19 Texas facilities publish. That share is a statement about disclosure as much as about size, since it is measured only against the facilities willing to state a number. The campus holds 347,000 square feet of technical space and a Green Globes certification, which covers energy efficiency operations rather than AI workload readiness.

The capacity becomes hardware only through assumption. At 40 kW per rack, 84 MW is roughly 2,100 racks. At 10 kW per GPU, it is about 8,400 high-end accelerators if the entire load went to GPU compute. Neither figure is published by the operator, and neither accounts for cooling, networking, or the power actually delivered to the site.

What the data does not cover is the binding question. No grid connection capacity, no interconnection status, and no announced expansion appear here, so whether this campus can sustain AI training loads is unknown. Texas's total data center capacity is also unknown, because the other 114 mapped facilities publish no power figures. The 84 MW is a floor on what Texas holds, not a measure of what it can deliver.
